name: Gestational Trophoblastic Disease, Hydatidiform Mole and Choriocarcinoma

reference.source: Sakshi Arora Obstetrics 9th Edition / FIGO Committee on Gynecologic Oncology
clinicalPearls: Complete hydatidiform mole is androgenetic diploid (46,XX) with absent p57 expression and diffuse villous hydropic swelling
Partial hydatidiform mole is diandric triploid (69,XXY) with fetal tissue present and positive p57 expression
Suction curettage under oxytocin infusion is the primary treatment of choice for molar evacuation
Weekly quantitative serum beta-hCG monitoring until three consecutive normal titers is mandatory post-evacuation
Choriocarcinoma is an aggressive avascular epithelial tumor metastasizing hematogenously to lungs and vagina, highly sensitive to chemotherapy
reference.pathophysiology: Gestational trophoblastic disease encompasses complete and partial hydatidiform moles, invasive moles, choriocarcinomas, and placental site trophoblastic tumors. Complete moles develop when an enucleated ovum is fertilized by a haploid sperm that duplicates its genome (or two sperm), resulting in purely paternal nuclear DNA, loss of maternal p57 cyclin-dependent kinase inhibitor expression, and diffuse trophoblastic hyperplasia. Choriocarcinoma consists of sheets of anaplastic syncytiotrophoblast and cytotrophoblast without formed chorionic villi.
additionalDifferentials: Threatened or incomplete miscarriage with hydropic degeneration
additionalInvestigations: Transvaginal pelvic ultrasound ('snowstorm' or 'bunch of grapes' appearance)
Chest radiography to screen for pulmonary metastases ('cannonball' lesions)
